title: Connector probe & sink throttling: healthchecks and graceful backpressure for OTLP->Tempo/Jaeger exporters
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Our OTLP connector that forwards spans to downstream backends (Tempo, Jaeger) currently retries and buffers with limited observability into downstream health. When a sink degrades (slow writes, error surge), the connector compounds load and increases end-to-end latency for customer traces. We need an operational layer on the connector to detect sink health regressions quickly and apply controlled backpressure / throttling policies to preserve platform SLOs and avoid noisy retries.

Goal:
Implement a lightweight probe & sink-throttling subsystem in the OTLP connector that: 1) probes each configured sink for liveness and write latency; 2) maintains a per-sink health state (healthy / degraded / offline); 3) exposes metrics and events for dashboards/alerts; 4) applies configurable throttling/circuit-breaker policies to slow down, batch, or shed low-priority traces when a sink is degraded; 5) supports automatic fallback to archival (S3/GCS) or alternate sink routing where configured.

Scope & Requirements:
- Add a periodic probe job per sink that performs a light-weight write or health-check path, measuring p50/p95/p999 write latency and error rate. Probes should be non-blocking and rate-limited.
- Health state machine: healthy -> degraded -> offline. Transition thresholds configurable per-sink (latency thresholds, error-rate windows, consecutive failures).
- Throttling policies: token-bucket shaped admission control + dynamic batch size adjustment. Support three preset modes: conservative, normal, aggressive (configurable via connector config).
- Graceful shedding: when in degraded/offline, mark low-value traces (e.g., diagnostic or internal spans) for asynchronous archival and prioritize customer-facing spans. Provide route tags/metadata to identify priority.
- Fallback routing: ability to route to secondary sink or archive bucket with metadata preservation.
- Metrics & alerts: emit metrics for probe latency/error, sink health state transitions, throttle rate, dropped/spilled spans, and fallback events. Create Prometheus metrics & OTLP metrics and structured logs for state transitions.
- Console/Dashboard: wire key metrics into the Console runtime tracing dashboard (latency heatmap, per-sink health panel, throttle impact chart). Suggested dashboard queries included in design doc.
- Safety: ensure circuit-breaker decisions are idempotent and avoid split-brain between connector shards. Persist minimal health cache to local disk to avoid transient flip-flops during restarts.
- Tests & QA: unit tests for state machine, integration tests with a fake slow Tempo backend, chaos test causing intermittent write failures and verifying fallback and SLA preservation.

Non-goals:
- Full multi-tenant quota-aware shedding (follow-up ticket).
- Rewriting the entire exporter pipeline; this sits as an operational shim in the connector layer.

Deliverables:
- Connector probe implementation + config schema
- Throttling/circuit-breaker module with policy presets
- Prometheus/OTLP metrics emitted by the connector
- Console dashboards + alert rules PR
- Integration test harness and a canary rollout plan

Acceptance criteria:
- Synthetic test: when fake sink injects 10x latency, connector moves sink to degraded in <60s and reduces outbound RPS by >=70% for low-priority traces without affecting priority traces beyond SLA.
- Metrics emitted and dashboard panels render in staging with correct labels per-sink.
- Can demonstrate automatic fallback to archive for shed traces and evidence of no unbounded memory growth under failure.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Aisha Patel: Draft spec added. Initial threshold suggestions: p95 > 500ms -> degraded, >2000ms or 5xx rate > 10% -> offline. Need engineering buy-in on thresholds and persistence strategy.

2026-03-02 - Marc Lopez: PoC started. Implemented probe loop and a simple state machine persisted to a local sqlite file. Observed frequent flip-flops in unit tests; added debounce window (30s) to transitions.

2026-03-05 - Priya Nair (SRE): Review feedback: suggest exposing probe success vs write success separately, and add a backpressure signal metric that Console can surface. Recommend conservative preset for initial rollout.

2026-03-08 - Marc Lopez: Integrated token-bucket admission control. Added config flags: throttle_mode, probe_interval_ms, latency_thresholds_ms, fallback_bucket_uri. Draft dashboard panels in PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/3281.

2026-03-10 - Sven Berg (Platform): Noted potential cross-shard split-brain if probe caches are not replicated. Agreed to persist last-known-state and use leader-election TTL for cluster-wide decisions (follow-up ENG-21490).

2026-03-12 - Marc Lopez: Integration tests passing against staging tempo-slower instance. Preparing rollout plan: canary on 5% of connectors for 48h, monitor throttle_rate and dropped_spans metrics. Creating alert runbooks.
